page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top with page number 144 at upper left. Main text in one column of short lines (litany-style list, each petition beginning with a capitalised word, grouped in stanzas). Marginal notes in the right margin: "Libera nos Domine" beside the first group, "Te rogamus audi nos" beside the second group, and "Ut nos" beside the last lines at the bottom right.

main_text.l: Per dulcorem & gaudiū de Christi incarnatione,
Per gaudium & lætitiam de ejus Ascensione,
Per gaudium & lætitiam de tua coronatione.
Ut sanctam Ecclesiam piissima co- servare digneris,
Ut justis gloriam, peccatoribus gra- tiam impetrare digneris.
Ut navigantibus portum, peregrinantibus reditum, infirmantibus sanitatem, tribulatis consolationem, captivis liberationem impetrare digneris.
Ut famulos & famulas tuas, tibi devote servientes confolari digneris.
Ut cunctum populum Christianum, filii tui preciofo sanguine redemptū, conservare digneris.
Ut cunctis fidelibus defunctis æternam requiem impetrare digneris.

page.notes: Right margin notes, as printed: "Libera nos Domine" (beside the first group, partly in black letter/ornamental type, reading "Libera nos Domine"); "Te rogamus audi nos" (partly illegible, read as "Te rogamus: audi nos", with "Te toga" and "mus:au" visible); "di nos" and "Ut nos" at the bottom right, the last partly cut off. Several words are doubtful due to the faded scan, notably "Ut cunctum", "Christianum" and the line ends of the litany; these are unverified. The notes are transcribed only as far as they are legible.
